structure.title: Act I – Act III, scene 2 · Sicilia · Jealousy catches up with its evidence
structure.text: Two old friends are visiting. When Hermione persuades the guest to stay, her husband Leontes treats the success of his own request as proof of adultery. Courtiers face a frightening task in correcting an interpretation that already has the force of law.

structure.title: Act III, scene 3 – Act IV · Bohemia · A child grows up
structure.text: The action leaves the palace for a shore, a shepherd's household and eventually a sheep-shearing feast. Sixteen years let a new generation develop attachments without knowing why their elders would object to them.

structure.title: Act V · The return · What time has done to a house
structure.text: The young couple's journey brings the two countries together again. People who remember the original accusations must decide what an account, a likeness or a work of art can establish after so long an absence.

people.name: Leontes
people.text: He asks his queen to persuade his oldest friend to stay longer, and she succeeds. Within minutes he has convinced himself that her success proves an affair, and a king's suspicion becomes everyone else's danger.

people.name: Hermione and Paulina
people.role: Queen and a friend willing to face the king
people.text: Hermione must defend herself before a husband who has claimed the right to judge. Paulina can say things the accused woman cannot and continues to insist that words have consequences after the hearing ends.

people.name: Perdita and Florizel
people.text: Their delight in one another belongs to the exuberant world of a country feast. Florizel's father has a very different understanding of what marriage requires of an heir.

context.title: Time takes the stage
context.text: The leap of sixteen years is announced by Time speaking as a character. A baby can come back as someone with her own opinions. For those who stayed at the palace the same interval has been a long adult experience of loss.

notice.text: When is an innocent gesture turned into a sign?
notice.why: Leontes can list touches and looks in impressive detail. Nearly everyone present saw the same meeting. His certainty grows at precisely the point where their accounts stop matching his.

notice.text: Look at the flowers at the sheep-shearing.
notice.why: Perdita distributes flowers by age and season, then argues about cultivation with a stranger. Her capacity to host a gathering brings her directly into conversation with someone who would deny her an equal place in his family.

opening: Leontes watches his wife persuade his oldest friend to prolong a visit and decides they must be lovers. Almost everyone around him sees an innocent exchange. Their objections only make him more certain that he alone understands what is happening. Shakespeare begins with the frightening speed of a private suspicion becoming public policy, then gives the consequences room to stretch across years. The play asks an unusual amount of time, affection, and imagination from the people left trying to live after a powerful man's certainty.
